observed_technique: A ConnectWise application granted itself Global Administrator, added client secrets to two other applications, and a new credential was later used to authenticate. Huntress observed Python-urllib/3.12 and secrets expiring in 2028.
sample_origin: Synthetic reconstructions of reported behavior using documented Graph APIs. No attacker source code was published. The SDK fixtures are equivalent future variants, not tooling attributed to this incident.

indicator_files.ENDPOINTS: All three hostile/suspicious IPs; no hostile hostname named.
indicator_files.SHA256: Empty: article supplies no sample hashes.
indicator_files.PURLS: Empty: article supplies no hostile package coordinates. The user agents identify common legitimate tools, not compromised package artifacts; requests/2.31 and urllib/3.12 are version scopes, not inferred patch versions.

excluded_feed_cves: CVE-2026-102764 and CVE-2026-105445 occur in related-article links, not this incident.
severity: Grant and credential-reuse sequence remains suspicious: authorized provisioning can perform the same operations. No malicious intent is inferred from SDK names, IPs, user agents, or vendor application IDs.
limitations: Role-ID proximity is co-occurrence, not proof the posted body contains that ID or that the role is self-assigned.
Credential reuse fields are co-occurrence, not proof of response-to-login data flow or successful authentication.
JavaScript chained api(path).post(body) is covered; a separately stored builder is not.
C# indexed AddPassword calls use anchored AST matching because the symbol target is unavailable.
No unconfirmed data theft, directory enumeration, payload execution, or certificate creation is reconstructed.
